lessons: Review snag only: scope fence, verification, run_record and diff_budget checks all passed. Keep the existing release, fold, refusal-case and dormancy work; fix just the idempotency gap.

Make the release identity terminal in `squatch/flake.py`. Before appending, `release` must return False if the journal already holds a `signal` keyed `flake-release/<box_id>/<fix_stem>`. Otherwise a re-detect after release lets the old fix's evidence release the test a second time.
Do not change detection's event contract (it is scoped out). Put the guard on the release side, not in `detect`. A re-quarantined report must then stay quarantined against the old fix_stem.

Add a test to `tests/test_flake.py`: release, then re-detect the same report, then release again with the same fix_stem and a green rerun. Assert no second release event and the entry still quarantined, both live and after reconstructing the journal.

Make sure `_fold_quarantine` still folds cleanly across the sequence detect -> release -> detect for the same box_id, with no JournalCorruption. Assert the final quarantine projection in the new test.
reason: A fixable oversight named by the review: a second release of the same identity after re-detection appends a duplicate event, and the paved road is concrete and within the fence.
